extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on types of story endings and quality criteria for writing effective, satisfying conclusions in fiction. Covers ending archetypes, what makes endings succeed or fail, and tests to evaluate an ending's strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution / Closed Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict resolved; loose ends tied; protagonist's arc complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most common in commercial fiction. Use when readers expect closure and narrative threads should be settled. Ensure resolution follows logically from story events rather than being abrupt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twist Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: A revelation reframes earlier events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality requires foreshadowing and an earned surprise. Risks include cheating the reader, an unmotivated twist, or being too telegraphed. Balance surprise with retrospective inevitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open / Ambiguous Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Key questions left for the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns with story's tone and theme and is common in literary fiction. Works best when ambiguity is thematically justified rather than lazy or accidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cliffhanger Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspends mid-action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Needs a sequel or payoff to feel honest. Risky in standalone short stories where it is often perceived as cheating; use when intentional serial continuation is planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-Circle / Frame Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns to opening (image, location, idea) but transformed by what happened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a satisfying symmetry and shows character/world change. Related to Save the Cat's 'Final Image.' Ensure the return is transformed, not merely repeated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epilogue / Time-Skip Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows the future after main events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for answering 'what happened to…' questions, but can feel tacked on. Use sparingly and make sure it adds meaningful closure rather than neat-but-empty updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dying-Fall / Diminuendo Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Quiet, deliberately anticlimactic; tone of acceptance or melancholy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common in literary stories (e.g., Chekhov, Carver). Best when the story's mood and theme call for restraint rather than dramatic finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragic Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Protagonist fails, dies, or suffers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aristotelian model that can provide catharsis. Ensure the tragedy is earned by character decisions and thematic logic, not arbitrary cruelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iron / Twist of Knife Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Cruel revelation that recontextualizes everything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivers a harsh final reframe (example: Du Maurier's 'Don't Look Now'). Use when tone and theme support a darker payoff and the recontextualization is fair to the setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refused Ending / Anti-Climax
rubrics_metrics.description: Story explicitly denies expected resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often experimental. Effective when purposeful (to make a point or unsettle); ineffective when it feels like avoidance of plotting or craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned, Not Arbitrary
rubrics_metrics.description: The ending must follow from setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reader should feel 'of course.' Avoid solutions that come from outside the story's established logic; the emotional and plot outcomes must be motivated by what precedes them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprising AND Inevitable
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal: surprise in the moment, inevitability in retrospect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for endings that shock but, on reflection, feel like the only authentic conclusion. Combine foreshadowing with misdirection that still respects established facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resonant
rubrics_metrics.description: Lingers; rewards reflection; invites re-reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A resonant ending leaves thematic or emotional echoes. Craft images, lines, or moments that stick and reveal more on a second read instead of resolving everything superficially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tonally Coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: Matches the story's overall mood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid tonal dissonance (e.g., a happy ending in a bleak story feels false). Ensure the ending's emotional register suits the narrative voice and stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Not rushed; not over-extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't cut the climax short or let the denouement drag. Pace the final scenes so emotional beats land without feeling hurried or padded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doesn't Explain
rubrics_metrics.description: Lets the reader feel meaning rather than have it stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid expository wrap-ups or information-dumps that tell rather than show. Trust the reader to infer implications from the final scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recontextualizes the Beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: Best endings change how the opening reads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong ending should throw earlier scenes into new light, revealing deeper meaning or irony. Use structural echoes or revelations to shift perspective on the opening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific, Not Generic
rubrics_metrics.description: A unique image, line, or moment — not 'and they all lived happily ever after.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End with specificity that anchors emotion and theme. Avoid clichés and blanket statements that flatten emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deus ex machina
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescue from outside the story's logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A common failure mode; avoid external rescues or last-minute contrivances that weren't foreshadowed. Solutions should arise from story elements already in play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author's-out endings (dream/waking device)
rubrics_metrics.description: Character wakes up / 'it was a dream' endings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seen as an author's-out; typically unsatisfying because they negate stakes and consequence. Use only when the device itself is thematically justified and signaled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unearned reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters reconcile without sufficient setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid sudden reconciliations that negate conflict without believable emotional work. Ensure shifts in relationships are motivated and shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information-dump explaining what happened
rubrics_metrics.description: Expository explanation of events at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: late-stage exposition that tells rather than shows. Prefer scenes that dramatize outcomes or let implications emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop without resolution (laziness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Abrupt stop that is different from a deliberate open ending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish purposeful ambiguity from sloppy stopping. A genuine open ending is crafted; a lazy stop lacks justification and leaves the reader frustrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Then everyone died" cynical default
rubrics_metrics.description: Using mass death as a cheap or cynical end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid this hackneyed route unless death is thematically integral and earned; otherwise it reads as a default rather than a meaningful choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequel-bait that prevents story from working alone
rubrics_metrics.description: An ending that exists mainly to set up future installments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure standalone satisfactions even if planning sequels. Sequel-bait is a failure mode when it denies closure the current story needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chosen, Not Stumbled Into (Quality Test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the ending feel chosen, not stumbled into?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the author made deliberate structural and thematic choices to reach the ending, rather than arriving by accident or convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential Loss with Alternate Ending Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Could this story have ended differently and lost something essential?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether changing the ending would diminish the story's meaning or impact. A strong ending should be integral, not interchangeable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Last Sentence Resonance Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the last sentence resonate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the potency of the final line: does it encapsulate theme, provide a striking image, or leave an emotional echo? The last sentence should carry weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-read Desire Test
rubrics_metrics.description: Would the reader want to re-read knowing the ending?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high-quality ending makes a reader want to revisit the story to catch foreshadowing or deeper meanings. If the ending undermines re-read value, it may be weak.
